classification.difficultyReason: Solve pairs of linear equations, including fractional intersection coordinates.

content.prompt: For each pair of equations, find the coordinates of the point where the lines intersect.

answer.worked:
Adding the equations:
$$\begin{align*}5x&=5\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(1)+y&=4\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(1,2)$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives $x=4$.

Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(4)-2y&=7\\8-2y&=7\\-2y&=-1\\y&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(4,\tfrac12)$.

Substituting $y=5+x$ into the second equation:
$$\begin{align*}2x-(5+x)&=3\\x-5&=3\\x&=8\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}y&=5+8\\y&=13\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(8,13)$.

Equating the expressions for $y$:
$$\begin{align*}2x-12&=-3x-2\\5x&=10\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(2)-12\\y&=-8\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(2,-8)$.

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ gives $3x-12y=39$. Subtracting this from the second equation:
$$\begin{align*}7y&=-21\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}x-4(-3)&=13\\x+12&=13\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(1,-3)$.

Multiplying the first equation by $4$ gives $8x+4y=16$. Adding the second equation:
$$\begin{align*}11x&=22\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(2)+y&=4\\y&=0\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(2,0)$.

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and the second by $2$ gives:
$$\begin{align*}6x-12y&=39\\6x-10y&=34\end{align*}$$
Subtracting the first resulting equation from the second:
$$\begin{align*}2y&=-5\\y&=-\frac52\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the original first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2x-4\left(-\frac52\right)&=13\\2x+10&=13\\2x&=3\\x&=\frac32\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(\tfrac32,-\tfrac52)$.

Substituting $y=5-9x$ into the second equation:
$$\begin{align*}5x-3(5-9x)&=1\\5x-15+27x&=1\\32x&=16\\x&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}y&=5-9\left(\frac12\right)\\y&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$.

Subtracting the second equation from the first:
$$\begin{align*}3y+2&=0\\3y&=-2\\y&=-\frac23\end{align*}$$
Substituting into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}x-3\left(-\frac23\right)+3&=0\\x+5&=0\\x&=-5\end{align*}$$
The intersection is $(-5,-\tfrac23)$.
